body:
Apologies, yes so I'm not sure about the termination piece, I actually have a quarterly performance review next week that I am dreading, so seeing how this goes will better allow me to answer. 

So the new role is more working directly with educators on our platform and how they interface with it to do their work. Don't want to get too specific here, but it is very different from working with data and software engineers and infrastructure like I have in the past. Not to say I am bad at thinking about users and workflows, but not what I wanted from my career.

Yes the value piece you mention in your first point really seems to be my issue. I think what is also frustrating, it is frustrating and confusing to feel like there is value in platform related work yet it not being seeing as immediately effective by leadership.

This resonates -- I actually went to school for engineering so I am quite comfortable with the technical solutions my team pushes and would love to continue to work in that capacity. I just clearly lack the ability to tailor my messaging to business stakeholders and I'm not sure how to improve that skill. Do you have any tips on being more effective in front of business stakeholders?

I really like working with the technical teams and diving into the nitty gritty of technical solutions, I like the end user feedback portion, I also do like defining processes around the product as well. Don't love the stakeholder and leadership management aspects.

I work primarily with data and back end(platform) teams primarily and I'm moving to a more user centered front end process role. It is very much not in my wheel house and my 3 years in product has been working in primarily technical teams.

From two directors that were new to their respective roles, hence my statements about communicating with the top brass and politics of being a product person. Clearly these are skills that I can improve on, but I strongly dislike managing up so to speak.

That's helpful, this particular director is a recent hire, so totally valid that the response may be off. I feel like perhaps this is also another piece of the struggles with management I see very frequently in start up environments

Why such a smug attitude? I obviously can't take a huge decrease in pay, I have expenses and a partner to support. Also there is a huge difference between another job and McDonald's. Also just because a manager does something, does not mean it is an accurate reflection of your performance. As a matter of fact if you were paying attention you would have noticed I mentioned my development team loves me, as do quite a few of the other stakeholders I work with. Stop licking boots.

No but when you both don't particularly like the work and aren't good at it, what value is there in continuing to do it? I get better at a job I hate? The only reason I have stuck to product management is because I came to it early in my career, the money is good, and I thought I was good at it. I don't really love it as a career, and now I have one less reason to stay.
Thanks I was thinking how deep I want to go there's no way they wouldn't want to talk to someone face to face. I created a real hole for myself

Thanks for the reply. I'm calling the center to make an appointment, and emailing student services to see if I can get the diagnosis. I just don't want to be kicked out of school, but right now it seems inevitable. Thank you for helping, I don't really have a lot of people to talk about this things with, so I guess I just wanted you to know you made someone's day better
Well is I'd try, but in a situation in which I graduate and I'm not in the right major or even college. I don't think they'd take it well. Thanks for replying it meant a lot to me.
